name: hub-bridge-target-agent
description: Telegram bridge with bridge_target_agent naming a non-coordinator agent: that agent runs the bridge, a new Telegram message wakes it, and its answer goes back to the chat once. The coordinator never sees the message. Fake Bot API (tests/tmux/lib/fake_telegram.py), fake model, throwaway HOME, no keyring.

config.command: sh -c 'R=$(pwd); H=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-bridge-target.path"); cd "$H/ws" && HOME="$H" KOLLAB_NO_KEYRING=1 PATH="$R/.venv/bin:$PATH" exec "$R/.venv/bin/python" "$R/tests/tmux/lib/fake_telegram.py" run "$H/tg.port" --no-daemon'

steps.description: throwaway HOME, fake model, fake Telegram bot, bridge_target_agent=lapis
steps.command: R=$(pwd); P="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-bridge-target.path"; [ -s "$P" ] && O=$(cat "$P") && { tmux kill-session -t '=kollab-spec-bridge-lapis' 2>/dev/null; kill "$(cat "$O/fake.pid")" "$(cat "$O/tg.pid")" 2>/dev/null; }; H=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-bridge-target.XXXXXX"); printf %s "$H" > "$P"; mkdir -p "$H/.kollab" "$H/ws"; touch "$H/.kollab/connect-guide-seen"; ("$R/.venv/bin/python" "$R/tests/tmux/lib/fake_llm.py" "$H/fake.port" >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > "$H/fake.pid"); ("$R/.venv/bin/python" "$R/tests/tmux/lib/fake_telegram.py" serve "$H/tg.port" >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > "$H/tg.pid"); for _ in $(seq 1 50); do [ -s "$H/fake.port" ] && [ -s "$H/tg.port" ] && break; sleep 0.3; done; printf '{"application":{"setup_completed":true},"kollabor":{"llm":{"active_profile":"fake","profiles":{"fake":{"provider":"custom","model":"fake-echo","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:%s/v1","api_key":"not-a-real-key"}}},"permissions":{"approval_mode":"trust_all"}},"plugins":{"hub":{"bridge_enabled":true,"bridge_platform":"telegram","bridge_token":"123:fake","bridge_chat_id":"42","bridge_target_agent":"lapis","bridge_poll_interval":1}}}' "$(cat "$H/fake.port")" > "$H/.kollab/config.json"; echo "fake model on $(cat "$H/fake.port"), fake telegram on $(cat "$H/tg.port")"

steps.description: lapis starts in its own pane; only lapis connects the bridge
steps.command: R=$(pwd); H=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-bridge-target.path"); tmux new-session -d -s kollab-spec-bridge-lapis -x 200 -y 50 "cd \"$H/ws\" && HOME=\"$H\" KOLLAB_NO_KEYRING=1 PATH=\"$R/.venv/bin:$PATH\" exec \"$R/.venv/bin/python\" \"$R/tests/tmux/lib/fake_telegram.py\" run \"$H/tg.port\" --no-daemon --as lapis"; for _ in $(seq 1 120); do grep -qs "telegram bridge connected" "$H"/.kollab/projects/*/logs/kollab.log && break; sleep 0.5; done; echo "bridge connections: $(grep -hc "telegram bridge connected" "$H"/.kollab/projects/*/logs/kollab.log)"

steps.description: the message reaches lapis and lapis takes a model turn
steps.command: H=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-bridge-target.path"); kill -USR1 "$(cat "$H/tg.pid")"; for _ in $(seq 1 60); do tmux capture-pane -p -t '=kollab-spec-bridge-lapis:' | grep -q "pong:" && break; sleep 0.5; done; tmux capture-pane -p -t '=kollab-spec-bridge-lapis:' | grep -E "Marco -> lapis|ping from telegram|pong:"

steps.description: the answer goes back to the chat exactly once
the coordinator never sees the message

steps.command: H=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-bridge-target.path"); tmux kill-session -t '=kollab-spec-bridge-lapis' 2>/dev/null; kill "$(cat "$H/fake.pid")" "$(cat "$H/tg.pid")" 2>/dev/null; echo "fakes stopped"
